paragraphs.context: Queen: Since the death of Queen Oasis, the tribe is split between
paragraphs.mainIdea: Three sisters want to be queen.
paragraphs.simple: Queen Oasis of the SandWings died. Now her three daughters, Burn, Blister and Blaze, all want her throne.

background.note: Queen Oasis was the SandWing queen before the war. After she died, her three daughters fought over her throne.
Burn is one of three SandWing sisters who are fighting to be queen. She is huge and violent.
Blister is one of three SandWing sisters who are fighting to be queen. She is clever and cold.
Blaze is one of three SandWing sisters who are fighting to be queen. She is friendly but not very clever.

paragraphs.context: Alliances: Burn fights alongside SkyWings and MudWings; Blister is allied with the
paragraphs.simple: Each SandWing sister has friends in other tribes. Burn has the SkyWings and MudWings, Blister has the SeaWings, and Blaze has the IceWings.

background.note: The desert dragons of Pyrrhia. They have pale gold scales and a poisonous barb on the end of the tail, and they can live a long time without water.
Silver-white or pale blue dragons from the frozen north of Pyrrhia. They can live in great cold and breathe out a deadly freezing breath (frostbreath).

paragraphs.context: Abilities: can breathe fire (if warm enough), hold their breath for up
paragraphs.simple: MudWings can breathe fire when they are warm, stay under water or mud for an hour without breathing, and hide in mud. They are very strong.

paragraphs.context: Abilities: powerful fighters and fliers, can breathe fire
paragraphs.simple: SkyWings are strong fighters and fast fliers, and they can breathe fire.

paragraphs.context: Description: blue or green or aquamarine scales; webs between their claws; gills
paragraphs.simple: SeaWings are blue or green. They have skin between their claws, gills for breathing under water, and stripes that glow in the dark.

paragraphs.context: Abilities: can withstand subzero temperatures and bright light, exhale a deadly freezing breath
paragraphs.simple: IceWings can live in very cold places and bright light, and they breathe out a deadly freezing breath.

paragraphs.context: Abilities: can camouflage their scales to blend into their surroundings, use their
paragraphs.simple: RainWings can change the colors of their scales to hide and can hold on to branches with their tails. The guide says they have no natural weapons.

paragraphs.context: Abilities: can breathe fire, disappear into dark shadows, read minds, foretell the future
paragraphs.simple: NightWings breathe fire and hide in shadows. The guide says they can read minds and see the future.

background.note: The power to hear what other dragons are thinking. The guide says NightWings have this power.

paragraphs.context: Queen: a closely guarded secret
paragraphs.mainIdea: The NightWing queen is a secret.
paragraphs.simple: Nobody outside the tribe knows who the NightWing queen is.

paragraphs.context: When the war has lasted twenty years …
paragraphs.simple: This line starts a poem, the Dragonet Prophecy. It says the dragonets will come after the war has lasted twenty years.

background.note: The old prophecy that says five dragonets hatched on the brightest night will end the war.

paragraphs.context: When the land is soaked in blood and tears …
paragraphs.mainIdea: A land full of blood and tears.
paragraphs.simple: The dragonets will also come when the land is full of blood and tears: when many dragons have died and many are sad.

paragraphs.context: Find the SeaWing egg of deepest blue.
paragraphs.simple: These lines tell which eggs to find. One is a dark blue SeaWing egg. "Wings of night" means that a NightWing dragonet will come too.

paragraphs.context: The largest egg in mountain high
paragraphs.simple: The biggest egg, from high in the mountains, will give a SkyWing ("wings of sky").

paragraphs.context: For wings of earth, search through the mud
paragraphs.simple: For a MudWing ("wings of earth"), look in the mud for a red egg, the color of dragon blood.

paragraphs.context: And hidden alone from the rival queens,
paragraphs.simple: A SandWing egg is waiting, hidden where the SandWing queens who fight each other cannot find it.

paragraphs.context: Of three queens who blister and blaze and burn,
paragraphs.simple: Three SandWing sisters want to be queen. Two of them will die. "Blister and blaze and burn" are words for burning, and also the names of the sisters.

background.note: Blister is one of three SandWing sisters who are fighting to be queen. She is clever and cold.
Blaze is one of three SandWing sisters who are fighting to be queen. She is friendly but not very clever.
Burn is one of three SandWing sisters who are fighting to be queen. She is huge and violent.

paragraphs.context: if she bows to a fate that is stronger and higher,
paragraphs.simple: The sister who lives will learn this: if she accepts a fate that is stronger and higher than her, she will have great power, the "wings of fire".

paragraphs.context: Five eggs to hatch on brightest night,
paragraphs.mainIdea: Five eggs on the brightest night.
paragraphs.simple: Five eggs will hatch on the brightest night, and the five dragons will be born to end the war.

background.note: A night when all three moons are full at the same time. The prophecy says the five dragonets will hatch on the brightest night.

paragraphs.context: It should have been a quiet night; they shouldn’t have seen anyone
paragraphs.simple: Reed and his MudWing brothers and sisters are on a night patrol on the mountain border. Sixteen days ago they lost their sister Crane in a battle.

background.note: Reed is Clay's brother and the leader of his brothers and sisters.
Crane was Clay's sister. She died in a battle.

paragraphs.context: Reed still couldn’t think about that battle without feeling a huge pit
paragraphs.simple: Reed is still very sad about Crane. He leads his four brothers and sisters as their bigwings, but it should have been their brother Clay, whose egg was stolen.

background.note: Clay is a MudWing, one of the five dragonets of the prophecy. He is big, kind and loyal.

paragraphs.context: “Did you hear that?” Umber whispered, darting up to fly beside him.
paragraphs.simple: Umber, the smallest of the brothers and sisters, is the best at noticing things. Reed always listens to him.

background.note: Umber is a MudWing, one of Clay's brothers. He is small and notices things.

paragraphs.context: Still, he twisted around to check on his brothers and sisters, calling
paragraphs.simple: Reed calls the others closer. Pheasant, Sora and Marsh fly in a tight group behind him.

background.note: Pheasant is Clay's sister, a MudWing.
Sora is Clay's sister, a MudWing.
Marsh is Clay's brother, a nervous MudWing.

paragraphs.context: But the only sound he heard was the SandWing general up ahead,
paragraphs.simple: The SandWing general in front is shouting so loudly that their secret patrol is not secret at all.

paragraphs.context: And that was when the nine ice dragons suddenly shot out of
paragraphs.simple: Suddenly nine IceWings fly very fast out of the forest and attack the SandWings.

background.note: Silver-white or pale blue dragons from the frozen north of Pyrrhia. They can live in great cold and breathe out a deadly freezing breath (frostbreath).

paragraphs.context: It was so fast, so calculated and swift and sudden, that two
paragraphs.simple: The attack is so fast and well planned that two SandWings fall, badly hurt, before Reed even understands what is happening.

paragraphs.context: He saw the hesitation on all their faces and caught himself wondering
paragraphs.simple: Reed sees that the others are not sure, and he wonders again whether Clay would be a better leader for them.

paragraphs.context: But no one said what they must be thinking — it’s a
paragraphs.simple: Nobody says it, but they all think this fight could kill them. Still, they follow Reed down into the battle.

paragraphs.context: Reed hated fighting IceWings. Their serrated claws seemed ten times sharper than
paragraphs.simple: Reed hates fighting IceWings. Their claws have edges like a saw, their thin tails sting, and their icy breath can kill.

paragraphs.context: He shot a burst of fire at the biggest IceWing, who was
paragraphs.simple: Reed breathes fire at the biggest IceWing. Then he fights another one that attacks his side, until it pulls away.

paragraphs.context: Reed spotted an IceWing diving toward Umber and leaped to knock his
paragraphs.simple: Reed knocks Umber out of the way and takes the hit himself. Pheasant pulls an IceWing off Sora, but it comes back to use its deadly breath.

background.note: The deadly freezing breath of IceWings; it can freeze and kill other dragons.

paragraphs.context: I can’t lose anyone else, Reed thought. It’ll kill me. He smashed
paragraphs.simple: Reed cannot bear to lose anyone else. He cuts the IceWing's throat, and she falls weakly into the dark forest.

paragraphs.context: “Retreat!” a voice suddenly howled. Reed’s heart jumped hopefully, thinking the IceWings
paragraphs.simple: Someone shouts "Retreat!" Reed hopes it is the IceWings, but it is the SandWing general.

paragraphs.context: “Retreat,” he echoed the general, grabbing Umber and pulling him back. “Fall
paragraphs.simple: Reed repeats the order, pulls Umber away and checks that all his brothers and sisters are still alive.

paragraphs.context: Reed saw the SandWings take off toward the mountains. Most of the
paragraphs.simple: The SandWings fly off toward the mountains. Most IceWings go very fast after them, but two turn to chase Reed and his family.

paragraphs.context: “This way!” he cried, diving for the forest. If IceWings could hide
paragraphs.simple: Reed leads his family into the forest. He does not have to follow the SandWings, and he does not want to lead the IceWings to his village.

background.note: The palace of the SkyWing queen, high in the mountains.

paragraphs.context: He heard the sound of thrashing wings farther back and risked a
paragraphs.simple: Reed looks back and sees that his brothers and sisters are all there. The noise must be IceWings stuck in the branches.

paragraphs.context: Silence fell. No one breathed. The branches creaked overhead, and small night
paragraphs.simple: They lie very still. Branches creak, small animals run past, and a squirrel runs over Reed's foot, but he does not move at all.

paragraphs.context: “I hate this war,” Umber burst out. “I don’t understand what we’re
paragraphs.simple: Umber suddenly says he hates the war. He does not know why he must fight for a SandWing queen he has never met.

background.note: Burn is one of three SandWing sisters who are fighting to be queen. She is huge and violent.

paragraphs.context: “Queen Moorhen must have a good reason for allying with Burn and
paragraphs.simple: Reed says Queen Moorhen must have a good reason for joining Burn and the SkyWings, and they should not doubt her.

background.note: Queen Moorhen is the queen of the MudWings.

paragraphs.context: There was something about the way she said Clay’s name that made
paragraphs.simple: Reed feels terrible. His siblings believe so much in Clay, and he wonders if they wish Clay were their leader. Maybe Crane would still be alive.

paragraphs.context: “Actually,” Pheasant said, “some dragons think it depends on when you start
paragraphs.simple: Pheasant explains that it depends on when you start counting: from the first battle it is eighteen years, but from Queen Oasis's death it is almost twenty.

background.note: Queen Oasis was the SandWing queen before the war. After she died, her three daughters fought over her throne.
A message that tells what will happen in the future. NightWings who can see the future give prophecies.

paragraphs.context: “If you’re all unhappy,” Reed said tentatively, “we could — I mean,
paragraphs.simple: Reed carefully says that they could try to find the Talons of Peace.

background.note: A secret group of dragons from different tribes who want to end the war. They raised the dragonets of the prophecy.

paragraphs.context: “You don’t have to decide tonight,” Pheasant said, more gently. “We just
paragraphs.simple: Pheasant says Reed does not have to decide tonight. They only just escaped, and they should go home and sleep.

paragraphs.context: “What were those IceWings doing here anyway?” Marsh asked, stamping his feet.
paragraphs.simple: Marsh stamps his feet and asks why the IceWings were there at all.

paragraphs.context: “I have no idea,” Reed said. “It seemed as though they were
paragraphs.simple: Reed thinks the IceWings were waiting to attack, but their patrol is not important. Maybe the IceWings were there for something else.

paragraphs.context: “I do, too,” Reed said. He looked up at the stars. Before
paragraphs.simple: Reed hopes Clay ends the war soon, before he has to choose between his tribe and keeping his family safe.

paragraphs.context: Starflight suspected that he might be dead, except that everything hurt so much.
paragraphs.simple: Starflight feels so much pain that he knows he is still alive. He cannot open his eyes, and his nose and throat hurt.

background.note: Starflight is a NightWing, one of the five dragonets of the prophecy. He is shy and very clever, and he loves reading scrolls.

paragraphs.context: Perhaps he was still under the mountain.
paragraphs.simple: Starflight wonders if he is still in the cave under the mountain and if everything was one long bad dream.

background.note: Morrowseer is a big, scary NightWing. Years ago he told the Talons of Peace about the Dragonet Prophecy.

paragraphs.context: But Starflight was sure he could remember the large NightWing taking him aside.
paragraphs.simple: Starflight remembers Morrowseer telling him that NightWings must lead and must make others fear them. He knows he could not invent that.

background.note: Purple-black dragons with silver scales under their wings, like a night sky full of stars. Many dragons believe they can read minds and see the future.

paragraphs.context: Was the SkyWing palace real? The dragonets captured before even tasting sunlight
paragraphs.simple: He remembers the SkyWing prison, the arena and Queen Scarlet, who wanted to watch him fight and die.

background.note: Queen Scarlet was the cruel queen of the SkyWings until she lost her throne. She liked to watch prisoners fight in her arena.

paragraphs.context: No, that had to be real, because Starflight remembered being “rescued” by the NightWings.
paragraphs.simple: The NightWings took Starflight away from the SkyWings. He watched his friends get smaller below him, and he felt torn in half.

paragraphs.context: There had been another stern lecture from Morrowseer.
paragraphs.simple: Morrowseer told Starflight that he must lead the dragonets and make them choose Blister as the SandWing queen.

background.note: Blister is one of three SandWing sisters who are fighting to be queen. She is clever and cold.

paragraphs.context: And then there was the Kingdom of the Sea.
paragraphs.simple: In the Kingdom of the Sea, his friends did not listen to Starflight or follow him.

background.note: The land of the SeaWings: the sea, its islands and the palaces under the water.

paragraphs.context: Another prison; another escape where Starflight did just about nothing to help.
paragraphs.simple: After another escape, the dragonets went to the rainforest. There they found two strange tunnels: one to the Kingdom of Sand and one to the NightWings' secret home.

background.note: The thick, hot, wet forest in Pyrrhia where the RainWings live. The books call the RainWings' home 'the rainforest'.
The desert land of the SandWings.

paragraphs.context: The memory of the rainforest was blurring.
paragraphs.simple: Starflight tries to remember. He was guarding the tunnel so the NightWings could not come through and attack the RainWings.

background.note: Dragons of the rainforest whose scales change colour. They can hide by matching the colours around them, and they can shoot venom from their fangs.

paragraphs.context: Right — guarding the hole. With Clay. Morning sunbeams flickering through the green
paragraphs.simple: Starflight was guarding the tunnel with Clay. Sunny and Tsunami were in the village, watching Glory try to become the RainWing queen.

background.note: Clay is a MudWing, one of the five dragonets of the prophecy. He is big, kind and loyal.
Sunny is a small SandWing, one of the five dragonets of the prophecy. She is cheerful and always hopes for the best.
Tsunami is a SeaWing princess, one of the five dragonets of the prophecy. She is brave and likes to be the leader.
Glory is a RainWing, one of the five dragonets of the prophecy. She can change the colour of her scales and shoot venom.

paragraphs.context: I love you, he would never say.
paragraphs.mainIdea: What Starflight wants to tell Sunny.
paragraphs.simple: Starflight loves Sunny, but he can never say it. He is afraid she will think he is cruel like the other NightWings.

paragraphs.context: And then she’d glanced up at him and smiled, and in Sunny’s
paragraphs.simple: When Sunny smiles at him, Starflight feels that he is fine just as he is. But she sees him only as a friend.

paragraphs.context: He’d been staring at the hole, wondering what the other NightWings were really like.
paragraphs.simple: Starflight wondered what the NightWings were really like, and if they would listen to him and like him even though he has no special powers.

paragraphs.context: In a heartbeat, dark wings had boiled out of the hole; dark
paragraphs.simple: Dark dragons came out of the hole, held his snout and hit him on the head. Then everything went dark.

paragraphs.context: Starflight jolted up with a yell.
paragraphs.simple: Someone throws freezing sea water over Starflight, and he wakes up.

paragraphs.context: Six or seven or maybe eight dark blurry shapes surrounded him.
paragraphs.simple: Starflight sees several dark dragonets around him. The air is smoky, and red light glows along the walls.

paragraphs.context: “You all have tiny RainWing brains,” said yet another voice.
paragraphs.mainIdea: Why they did not pick a girl.
paragraphs.simple: One dragonet says that Starflight was still in his egg when he was chosen, so nobody knew what he would be like.

paragraphs.context: One of the shapes came close enough for him to make out
paragraphs.simple: An older dragonet looks at Starflight's teeth, chest and claws, and decides that he is weak.

paragraphs.context: “That’s Fierceteeth,” said the friendlier dragonet to Starflight.
paragraphs.simple: The friendly dragonet says his name is Mightyclaws. The unfriendly one is Fierceteeth, and she is Starflight's older sister.

background.note: Mightyclaws is a young NightWing who is friendly to Starflight.
Fierceteeth is Starflight's sister, a proud young NightWing.

paragraphs.context: “What part of brightest night are you having trouble with?”
paragraphs.simple: Another dragonet, Mindreader, says she will "stay out of his head". The older dragonets laugh as if it is a great joke.

background.note: Mindreader is a young NightWing. Her name means 'a dragon who can read minds'.
A night when all three moons are full at the same time. The prophecy says the five dragonets will hatch on the brightest night.

paragraphs.context: Now that his sight was clearing, he could see that he was
paragraphs.simple: Starflight is in a long cave with many beds cut into the rock. It looks like a dormitory, not a prison.

paragraphs.context: There were at least fifty sleeping spots that Starflight could see, but
paragraphs.simple: There are beds for fifty dragonets, but only about eleven are used.

paragraphs.context: Maybe there is something wrong with my tribe, Starflight thought.
paragraphs.mainIdea: Something is wrong with the tribe.
paragraphs.simple: Starflight thinks the NightWings may be losing their dragonets, or not having enough of them.

paragraphs.context: Everything smelled like sulfur and decaying animals.
paragraphs.simple: Everything smells of sulfur and dead animals, and the dragonets have very bad breath.

paragraphs.context: They were also shockingly thin, every one of them, with narrow chests
paragraphs.simple: The dragonets are all very thin, with red eyes and bad coughs.

paragraphs.context: He stretched gingerly, eyeing the door.
paragraphs.simple: The door is open, but Starflight thinks there must be guards, or something worse, outside.

background.note: Queen Coral is the queen of the SeaWings and Tsunami's mother.

paragraphs.context: “I want to hear about the mainland,” Mindreader said eagerly.
paragraphs.simple: Mindreader wants to hear all about the mainland. The young NightWings have never seen tall trees or a blue sky.

background.note: The main part of Pyrrhia, seen from the NightWings' island across the sea.

paragraphs.context: “Dragonets aren’t allowed to leave the island until we’re ten years old,” Mightyclaws said.
paragraphs.simple: NightWing dragonets cannot leave the island until they are ten years old, so that they do not tell the tribe's secrets.

paragraphs.context: Immediately the dragonets scattered to their sleeping spots.
paragraphs.simple: A small dragonet runs in to warn them. The others quickly pretend to sleep or read.

paragraphs.context: “Up,” he snarled. “The queen of the NightWings wants to see you.”
paragraphs.mainIdea: The queen wants to see him.
paragraphs.simple: Morrowseer comes in and tells Starflight that the NightWing queen wants to see him.

paragraphs.context: Starflight’s experience with dragon queens thus far had not been exactly wonderful.
paragraphs.simple: Starflight has met dragon queens before, and it was always bad for him.

paragraphs.context: Starflight’s claws caught on small holes in the rocky floor and he
paragraphs.simple: The walls are made of volcanic rock. The floor shakes and is hot, so Starflight thinks the volcano could erupt again.

paragraphs.context: Finally Morrowseer and Starflight stepped through an archway into a cave full of dragons.
paragraphs.simple: Morrowseer takes Starflight into a cave full of NightWings. They hang from the walls like bats and all stop talking to look at him.

paragraphs.context: A few steps into the cave, the rocky path abruptly fell away
paragraphs.simple: Starflight has to stand on a thin piece of rock. All around and below it is a lake of hot lava.

paragraphs.context: And they’re all reading my mind, he thought with another jolt of terror.
paragraphs.mainIdea: Afraid they can read his mind.
paragraphs.simple: Starflight thinks the NightWings are reading his thoughts, so he tries hard not to think about anything secret.

background.note: The power to hear what other dragons are thinking. The guide says NightWings have this power.

paragraphs.context: First, there weren’t actually hundreds of dragons staring at him.
paragraphs.simple: About forty old NightWings are in the cave. Like the dragonets, they are very thin and look ill, with sores on their scales.

paragraphs.context: There was a clear spot on the cave walls right across from him.
paragraphs.simple: In the wall there is a big round screen of stone, full of small holes. The NightWings keep looking at it.

paragraphs.context: On a ledge beside the circle perched a dragon with a scar
paragraphs.simple: A dragon with a scar and drooping wings sits next to the circle. She wears diamonds, but she does not look like a strong queen.

paragraphs.context: It took him only a moment of puzzling this out before he
paragraphs.simple: Starflight understands that the queen is behind the screen, watching him through the holes. Nobody can see her.

paragraphs.context: “And how did that RainWing escape?”
paragraphs.mainIdea: They talk about Glory and Clay.
paragraphs.simple: The NightWings are angry because a RainWing and a MudWing came to their island and escaped.

paragraphs.context: “That’s the RainWing I warned you about,” Morrowseer snarled.
paragraphs.simple: Morrowseer says Glory was the RainWing that the Talons of Peace took instead of a SkyWing dragonet. He had told them to kill her.

background.note: A secret group of dragons from different tribes who want to end the war. They raised the dragonets of the prophecy.

paragraphs.context: “She knows about the tunnel between our kingdoms,” challenged a dragon from
paragraphs.simple: The NightWings are afraid the RainWings will learn their plan, because Glory knows about the tunnel and saw their fortress.

paragraphs.context: “Queen Battlewinner says to shut up and ask him.”
paragraphs.simple: The diamond dragon passes on the queen's words: make the dragonet tell them what his friends know and plan.

background.note: Queen Battlewinner is the queen of the NightWings. Other tribes do not even know who she is.

paragraphs.context: Should he tell them Glory’s plan?
paragraphs.simple: Starflight does not know what to do. If he tells them Glory's plan, he betrays his friends. If he does not, he betrays his tribe.

paragraphs.context: This is the chance you wanted.
paragraphs.simple: Starflight wanted to talk to the NightWings and find a peaceful answer, but now he cannot find the right words.

paragraphs.context: This met with such an uproar that Starflight had to sit down
paragraphs.simple: Starflight says yes, the RainWings may attack. The NightWings shout, and he feels he has said the worst thing.

paragraphs.context: A horribly disfigured dragon pushed past Morrowseer, slithered into the cave, and
paragraphs.simple: A dragon with a terrible scar on his face comes in. The scar has melted his scales and closed one of his nostrils.

paragraphs.context: “Yeah, I noticed,” he hissed. “And yet I know more than any
paragraphs.simple: Vengeance says a RainWing queen sprayed him with venom by accident. He thinks RainWings are too lazy and weak to be dangerous.

background.note: Vengeance is a NightWing who was hurt by RainWing venom.
The large land (continent) where all the dragon tribes in these books live.

paragraphs.context: “And it’s your fault they found out about us,” the diamond dragon said.
paragraphs.simple: The diamond dragon says it is Vengeance's fault that Glory found the island, because he brought her there.

background.note: Deathbringer is a NightWing assassin: his job is to kill dragons when he is told to.

paragraphs.context: “Deathbringer.” Vengeance smirked. “Oh, yeah. How is your pet, Greatness? I’ve heard
paragraphs.simple: Vengeance calls Deathbringer the "pet" of Greatness and makes the guards drag him in.

background.note: Princess Greatness is a NightWing princess.

paragraphs.context: Deathbringer wasn’t much bigger than Starflight, after all — he’d looked larger when
paragraphs.simple: Deathbringer is not much bigger than Starflight. Here, in danger like Starflight, he does not look scary.

background.note: Blaze is one of three SandWing sisters who are fighting to be queen. She is friendly but not very clever.

paragraphs.context: “This dragon,” Vengeance bellowed, pointing at Deathbringer.
paragraphs.simple: Vengeance says Deathbringer helped the MudWing and the RainWing to escape.

paragraphs.context: Princess, Starflight thought. So the diamond dragon — Greatness — speaks for her mother
paragraphs.mainIdea: The diamond dragon is a princess.
paragraphs.simple: Starflight learns that the diamond dragon is Princess Greatness. She speaks for her mother, the queen.

paragraphs.context: A terrible silence followed. Starflight wondered whether they were all searching Deathbringer’s
paragraphs.simple: Everyone is quiet. Starflight thinks they are searching Deathbringer's mind, so he keeps his own mind empty.

paragraphs.context: Deathbringer glanced under his wing and met Starflight’s eyes.
paragraphs.simple: Deathbringer silently asks if the dragonets are still alive. Starflight nods a tiny bit, and Deathbringer looks relieved.

paragraphs.context: “Vengeance!” Greatness shouted, cutting him off. She stood up on her ledge
paragraphs.simple: Greatness stands up and tries to look scary and royal, but it looks like acting.

paragraphs.context: “The queen has spoken,” Greatness said into the perilous silence.
paragraphs.simple: The queen says Vengeance put the whole tribe in danger. He brought Glory, who is dangerous, as if she were a harmless RainWing.

paragraphs.context: “NO!” shrieked Vengeance. His wings flapped open, but he’d barely lifted off
paragraphs.simple: The guards grab Vengeance and throw him into the lake of lava.

paragraphs.context: Deathbringer shot up and out of the way as lava splashed all around them.
paragraphs.simple: A drop of hot lava lands on Starflight's foot. It hurts so much that he nearly faints.

paragraphs.context: Deathbringer’s talons yanked Starflight into the air just in time.
paragraphs.simple: Deathbringer pulls Starflight up into the air, away from the lava.

paragraphs.context: It was these spears they used to shove Vengeance back under the
paragraphs.simple: The guards push Vengeance under the lava with their spears until he sinks and is gone.

paragraphs.context: After a long moment, Starflight remembered to breathe again.
paragraphs.simple: Deathbringer looks worried, as if he has seen what could happen to him too.

paragraphs.context: “Don’t, Deathbringer,” Greatness said, her voice cracking.
paragraphs.simple: Greatness tells the guards to take Deathbringer to the dungeon. The queen will decide what to do with him later.

paragraphs.context: Greatness rubbed the ridges above her eyes, looking tired.
paragraphs.simple: Greatness ends the meeting. The NightWings must come back at dusk with plans to attack or to defend themselves.

paragraphs.context: They emerged onto a shelf of rock that jutted from the side
paragraphs.simple: Outside the fortress there is a field of gray-black rock with hot orange lava glowing in the cracks.

paragraphs.context: He remembered a little about volcanoes from one of the scrolls he’d
paragraphs.simple: Starflight did not know NightWings live on a volcano. There are no active volcanoes on the mainland.

background.note: The main part of Pyrrhia, seen from the NightWings' island across the sea.

paragraphs.context: Far overhead in the ashy sky, a pair of black dragons wheeled
paragraphs.simple: Starflight wonders how far the island is from the rest of Pyrrhia, and if the NightWings can travel there without the magic tunnels.

background.note: An animus is a rare dragon who can put magic into things or make magic happen with a spell. "Animus-made" tunnels were made with this magic.

paragraphs.context: But it didn’t feel true. This awful place was nothing like the
paragraphs.simple: Starflight imagined a beautiful NightWing home full of art, music and libraries. This place is smoky, ugly and unfriendly.

paragraphs.context: “J-just, um,” Starflight said. “I just want you to know I
paragraphs.simple: Starflight says he knows nothing more. But his mind thinks about Glory becoming queen, so he tries to think only of lava.

paragraphs.context: “Of course it isn’t,” Morrowseer snapped.
paragraphs.simple: Dragons who tried to land on the lava field fell through and died. Starflight sees their skulls.

paragraphs.context: Morrowseer hissed. “There’s a rotating schedule. All NightWings are allowed to hunt
paragraphs.simple: NightWings can hunt for only about five days each month. Morrowseer says he does not have to follow this rule.

paragraphs.context: “Naturally?” Starflight echoed, although he hadn’t meant for it to sound so
paragraphs.simple: Starflight thinks the NightWings must be running out of food on the island. That is why they are so thin.

paragraphs.context: Oh. That must be another reason they’re so angry right now — they’ve
paragraphs.simple: Starflight guesses the NightWings have been hunting in the rainforest. That is another reason they are angry now.

paragraphs.context: “You mean, covered with trees?” Starflight asked. “What happened? The volcano?” Stupid
paragraphs.simple: Lava from the volcano once covered almost all the trees on the island.

paragraphs.context: The older dragon landed with a thud that sent gray dust billowing
paragraphs.simple: Morrowseer runs around with his nose on the ground, sniffing loudly.

paragraphs.context: Starflight had never seen hunting like this.
paragraphs.mainIdea: How Dune taught them to hunt.
paragraphs.simple: Their guardian Dune taught them to hunt quietly and attack fast. Morrowseer's way is very different.

background.note: Dune was a SandWing guardian who raised the dragonets.

paragraphs.context: He followed the large black dragon, thinking about Dune and his hunting lessons.
paragraphs.simple: Dune was not very kind, but he was not as cruel as Kestrel, and he helped Starflight study.

background.note: Kestrel was a SkyWing guardian who raised the dragonets. She was strict and fierce.

paragraphs.context: More than half dead, Starflight thought.
paragraphs.simple: Under a bush there is a big gray and white bird that is almost dead.

paragraphs.context: As Morrowseer prodded it a few more times, Starflight spotted a bite
paragraphs.simple: The bird has a bite on its neck, like the dead sloth Starflight saw in the rainforest. The wound is infected.

paragraphs.context: Morrowseer gave him a dark look.
paragraphs.simple: Morrowseer says NightWings never get sick. He thinks Starflight is weak.

paragraphs.context: “You bite your prey,” he said slowly.
paragraphs.simple: Starflight understands: NightWings bite their prey, wait for it to die, then eat it when it is rotting. Something in their mouths kills the animals.

paragraphs.context: Morrowseer shook his head. “Some NightWings think so, but none of our
paragraphs.simple: Morrowseer says NightWing scientists have not found venom. They also cannot copy the way RainWings shoot venom.

background.note: Poison made by an animal. RainWings can shoot venom from their fangs that melts whatever it hits; SandWings have poison in the barb on their tail.

paragraphs.context: “I’m starting to see why you’re so useless,” Morrowseer hissed.
paragraphs.simple: Morrowseer says nobody taught Starflight to be a NightWing. He tells him to eat the rotten wing or go hungry.

paragraphs.context: “Listen, it might not make you sick, but I think it would
paragraphs.simple: Starflight explains in a scientific way that his body is not used to rotten meat, so it could make him sick.

sentences.context: If this dragon did suddenly spray venom at them, he wouldn’t blame her — but he didn’t want to be in the way when it happened.

sentences.grammar: "What Fatespeaker had said" is a noun clause used as the subject. "Sink in" = be slowly understood. "Not ... until" = only at that moment, not before. "A short flight from" = not far (for a flying dragon).

sentences.context: He couldn’t outfly them for long either — Flame, like most SkyWings, had enormous wings, which made them faster than dragons from any other tribe.

sentences.grammar: "Out-" + verb means "do it better than": outfly = fly faster than. "Either" after a negative = "also not". "Which" adds more about the wings.

sentences.context: There are dragonets who want their mothers and fathers to come home, and they know we’re the ones who’ll make it happen.

sentences.grammar: "Instead of ..." = and not. "That was trapped ... and kept ..." is a relative clause with two passive verbs. A "niche" is a small hole in a wall.
